PI-01.notes: Mechanism verified: every predictive family's log-likelihood equals scipy (normal, student-t, Poisson with exposure, negative binomial, Bernoulli, categorical, discrete hazard vs geometric), predictions are action-conditioned and registered at two horizons on the real Qwen3-4B configuration, and they change when only experiential weights change (max relative change of the predicted means 0.15 % / 7.6 % for perturbations of 5 % / 50 % of each tensor's std; adapters, heads and reward bit-identical). Learning evidence is debug-scale only (B's 86 measured numbers bit-reproduce on the committed code); on new mechanisms the heads do not beat the action-independent baseline; nothing is trained on the real configuration; not called by the runtime.
evidence: B suite on the HEAD snapshot with CAM_LIVE_B_MEASURE: 142 passed, 86/86 measured values equal docs/evidence/B/measured.json

PI-02.notes: PredictionRegistry refuses re-registration (edit), predictions dated after the registry clock, resolutions at or before registration, second resolutions; mutating the caller's object does not change the stored record; editing the log is detected; resolved NLL equals scipy. On the real configuration every lab.act prediction is in the registry with made_at == clock when evaluate_candidates returns. Limits: observed_at is supplied by whoever builds the observation; registry is single-writer.

PI-03.notes: Targets are built only from matured observed outcomes (build_targets masks pending / unobservable / missing / censored counts, refuses imagined); likelihoods correct. Training has run only with predict.labdata.train (plain Adam) at debug scale, not under the continual learner and not on the real configuration (B states this).
evidence: .venv/bin/python -m pytest cam_live/tests/predict -m 'not gpu and not slow' -q --rootdir=cam_live

PI-04.notes: Two horizons (6 h, 2 d) predicted and registered per candidate on the real configuration (2 records per lab.act candidate); horizon is a continuous input. More horizons only measured as an API property.

PI-05.notes: Epistemic (ensemble + fast posterior) and aleatoric parts are reported; epistemic_std > 0 on every real-configuration prediction; B's tests that epistemic uncertainty shrinks with data pass when re-run. Not measured by anyone: calibration of the combined uncertainty on the real model.
evidence: .venv/bin/python -m pytest cam_live/tests/predict -m 'not gpu and not slow' -q --rootdir=cam_live

PI-06.notes: Pending, unobservable and missing outcomes are masked with y left at 0 and mask False (never filled); censored non-time-to-event outcomes are masked; an imagined observation raises; a pending objective gives exactly zero evaluator loss and gradient. Minor: targets are stored as float32 (world.py:138).

PI-07.notes: Agrees with B's own 'partial': the planner exists and its outputs are flagged imagined, but the latent transition is worse than predicting the mean on held-out real transitions, the horizon never exceeds one step, and no decision comparison with/without planning exists. Not independently re-measured beyond B's re-run tests.
evidence: .venv/bin/python -m pytest cam_live/tests/predict -m 'not gpu and not slow' -q --rootdir=cam_live

PI-08.notes: For policy, greedy, UCB, VOI-weighted and Thompson (posterior samples and normal marginals) the recorded Decision.probabilities are what the index is drawn from (chi-square p 0.055-0.93 over 20000 draws each), the infeasible candidate gets exactly 0, the eps floor holds; the mean Thompson propensity from normal marginals matches the true P(best) within 0.01; randomised assignment matches the recorded 0.3/0.7 within 4 se and is registered before the first assignment. Gaps (B's own): rules not compared on a task beyond greedy vs VOI. On the real configuration an experiential-only change moves the decision distribution (Thompson TV 0.061 at a 5 % perturbation; greedy/UCB argmax flips, TV 0.98, at 50 %; policy-rule TV only 8e-5 / 8.5e-4 because the policy head is near-uniform at initialisation).

PI-09.notes: On real Qwen3-4B the proposer produced 4 schema-valid backbone actions merged with 13 schema-walker candidates, every candidate carries its provenance and decisions record exact probabilities. But the backbone is NOT conditioned on the latent in effect: log p(completion | prompt, b) is bit-identical for two different beliefs at initialisation (bridge output projection zero); the path exists (|dlogp| = 0.87 after perturbing the bridge) and only D's consequence provider (credit/providers.py:632) can train it. Proposal usefulness not measured.

PI-10.notes: Imagined objects (imagined flag / imagined_horizon_steps) are refused by build_targets, the registry and the evaluator path (B tests + own probe). Residual risk B states itself: code outside B could wrap an imagined value in an ordinary observation. C's ledger screen does not read an OutcomeObservation.imagined field (the field is being added to the contract in the working tree).

SE-01.notes: GoalEvaluator on the shared latent; success loss equals BCE-with-logits exactly; heads exist and run on the real configuration (B gpu evidence). Debug-scale training only.

SE-02.notes: prefix_targets applies one signed outcome to every earlier prefix (prefixes at/after evaluation masked, 1/n weight per trajectory); unsigned refused; pending -> zero loss and gradient; an 80 % forecast that fails receives gradient p - y. Integration (who calls EvaluatorLoss.add_outcome) is open.

SE-03.notes: Count magnitudes by negative binomial (== scipy, -> Poisson), time to achievement by a censoring-aware discrete hazard (== geometric; censored = survival of completed bins), resources by a normal on log1p. Accuracy only at debug scale.

SE-04.notes: Brier, NLL, reliability and slope/intercept are computed correctly on synthetic data with known calibration (true 0.7/0.3 inside the intervals) and predictions are prospective. DEFECT D5: the slope/intercept intervals ignore clustering (Brier/NLL use clusters): on a clustered null (40 lifetimes x 16 forecasts, true slope 0) the 95 % interval excludes 0 in 61 % of runs, so B's reported 'slope 254.16 (CI 122.43..385.90)' is not a valid interval. The trained evaluator does not beat the base rate (B).

SE-05.notes: action_quality = q[chosen] - E_pi q, regret, and quality + luck = surprise hold exactly; a lucky success of a poor decision has quality < 0, luck > 0. B reports that the raw outcome is the better indicator of true advantage at debug scale.

SE-06.notes: Reference VOI estimators are correct (E[max affine] and the knowledge gradient vs Monte Carlo; a decision-irrelevant observation with large surprise has VOI exactly 0) and the Predictor uses the Jensen gap E[max] - max E. Not done (B's own): the probe is not valued above the noisy gauge, VOI-aware selection did not beat greedy, the learned downstream estimator has no loss provider.

AE-01.notes: propose_experiment picks the least-certain ordered pair; select_experiment registers question, hypothesis and copies of the predictions before the first assignment, refuses infeasible arms, and assignment frequencies match the recorded probabilities. Hypotheses only restate predictions; analyse/conclude are left to the agent loop.

CU-12.notes: Candidates are generated from discovered tool descriptors (schema walker + real backbone, provenance merged) on LabWorld tools; not measured on the harness's discover_tools() output; multi-step programs from the real backbone not observed; latent conditioning ineffective at initialisation (see PI-09).

MR-01.notes: R_psi rewards every real decision of the debug model in LabWorld; intrinsic_reward, bootstrap_reward and reward_version are written to the record. Most predict-derived signals were masked in the runs (C states this); not wired into the agent.

MR-02.notes: psi is changed only by applied meta-updates (psi hash changes on an applied update, bit-identical on skips and policy updates); 20 applied meta-updates per seed in 80 reproduced LabWorld lifetimes. Trainable is not useful: see MR-05/MR-09.

MR-03.notes: MetaLearner.policy_update equals my own K=2 SGD on the documented loss driven by R_psi (max |diff| 1.1e-7 vs update 1.7e-2); the reward enters the update (meta-gradient through it non-zero, exactly 0 when R_psi is detached).

MR-04.notes: Independent torch.func implementation (nested grad, value baseline held fixed only for the inner derivative, per-group clip) agrees with C's engine to 1e-15 for K = 1, 2, 4, 8 on the real adaptable subset (62,211 parameters, 30,049 psi) and on a small configuration; K = 8 on the real subset was not in C's evidence and holds.

MR-05.notes: The applied meta-gradient equals my recomputation from the episodes (rel 1.8e-7); importance weighting is unbiased with logged propensities (MC |z| 2.2) and biased with wrong ones; refusals (missing / invalid / below-floor propensities, ESS, unverified) give no gradient and leave psi bit-identical; the inner-data score term is exact (enumerated). DEFECT D1 (major): with utility='return_to_go' (default) and verifier measurements, a row's leave-group-out baseline contains its own measured outcome (d b / d own outcome = 0.28 at row 2 of 8), so the outer gradient is biased. D7 (minor): cold start switches to the on-policy estimator within a 1e-3 tolerance. The LabWorld experiment's learned reward hurt (reproduced).

MR-06.notes: Unsigned, forged, replayed, invented and prediction-sourced outcomes are rejected and the ledger is hash-chained. DEFECT D2 (major): a validly signed outcome is admitted with any caller-chosen utility (1e6 for a signed value of 14) and credited to any exp_ids, so the utility number that supervises psi is not authenticated. DEFECT D3 (major): exclusion of self-generated goals depends on a caller argument objective_origin that defaults to OPERATOR; a verifier-signed outcome of a self-generated task is admitted by default.

MR-07.notes: Own reference: torch.func dJ/dpsi vs central FD on all 73 psi coordinates (rel <= 3.3e-9) for K = 1, 2, 4, 8 and on 43 sampled coordinates of the real subset (rel <= 1.6e-7) plus directional FD; C's engine (unroll and checkpoint) equals it to ~1e-15; C's own numbers reproduce exactly on the committed code (real subset 9.52e-6 / 9.56e-6 / 9.63e-6, |g| to 5 digits; tabular J and FD agreement for K = 1..8).

MR-08.notes: Bootstrap mode needs no pretraining, every record and MetaUpdateRecord carries the bootstrap label/mix, the shadow meta-update uses logged propensities (log(decision.probabilities[chosen]) to float32 precision). Minor: the label 'learned' is used for mix 0 even before any meta-update (bootstrap.py:182). The cold-start path showed no detectable benefit (C).

MR-09.notes: Tests exist and execute (C suite 115 passed). Guards hold for magnitude inflation (bounded; r -> 50 r leaves the update unchanged), duplicates, forged / unsigned / invented outcomes, ledger edits. Successful attacks: caller-chosen utility (D2), default-open self-goal origin (D3), paraphrased self-goals not discounted (D6), ledger truncation undetected by verify_chain (D8); the learned reward paid the noisy gauge in C's own experiment (reproduced collapse on seed 11).

MR-10.notes: Meta-updates are skipped with a recorded reason until enough independent verified groups exist and query rows without logged propensities never supervise. Within one lifetime the return-to-go utilities of different decisions are counted as independent groups while their baselines share outcomes (D1); only LabWorld multi-lifetime runs exercised it; no live/staging experience.

MR-11.notes: psi bit-identical after the live policy update and after skipped meta-updates; the reward optimizer holds exactly psi; R_psi detached in the learner loss. Minor: a truncated ledger file still has a valid chain (only a recorded head reveals it). Guards are in-process, not isolation.

AE-04.notes: DEFECT D4 (major): the goal-free budget is not enforced for goals that are selected but not yet resolved: SelfGoalSelector.select(k=5) returns 5 goals under a 2-decision budget and six successive selections while goals are pending return 6 (unbounded); can_afford checks each candidate alone and the budget is charged only on record_result/resolve. Spec 11.4: no unbounded activity outside the fixed budget. Also not called by the runtime; transfer is a constant (C).
